fatal_errors: The proposed intervention—incorporating an HEA—is circular because the starting catalyst is already a nearly equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy.
No specific compositional, synthetic, ageing, or discovery intervention is defined, so the modified catalyst cannot be reproduced.
The supporting evidence concerns electrocatalysis, ammonia decomposition, and nitrobenzene hydrogenation rather than aged automotive-exhaust catalysis under H2O/NO-containing feeds.
The falsification experiment lacks a defined exhaust composition, ageing protocol, temperature program, quantitative performance thresholds, and controlled platinum-group-metal loading.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad goals of improved activity, durability, and reduced platinum-group-metal use, but it does not reconstruct the central intervention: closed-loop high-throughput synthesis and post-ageing screening with machine-learning/Bayesian selection of composition and solvothermal processing conditions. It also omits the decisive high-alkalinity, moderately low-temperature synthesis window and the post-ageing Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction mechanism. The generic appeal to HEA synergy and thermal stability is scientifically plausible in other reactions but does not establish performance in three-way automotive catalysis. Predicted outcomes are qualitative and are not benchmarked against Pd using T50, conversion at 350 °C, or integrated conversion. The proposed comparison could in principle test a fully specified material, but as written neither the intervention nor the test conditions are operationally defined.
